purpose: The three tokensave definitions present on the reference machine before any Phase-C change. Sanitised. This is the 'before' state the repair actions are measured against, and the shape data the schema adapter must round-trip.

surfaces.name: VS Code user MCP
notes: Distinct top-level key ('servers', not 'mcpServers') plus a sibling 'inputs' array and a per-entry 'type' discriminator. This is the only one of the three needing a schema adapter.
Bare 'serve' with no -p. Structurally identical to the Claude Desktop entry retired in PR #18 (e9db057), but the VERDICT is pending A0: a fallback that never wins for a bound project is not broken.
File is tab-indented plain JSON here; JSONC tolerance is UNPROVEN and must be verified before choosing a parser.

surfaces.name: Copilot Agent Host user MCP
notes: Shares the 'mcpServers' key with Claude Code's .mcp.json, so the existing classifier may handle it with little or no adaptation.
Carries a per-entry 'type' field that .mcp.json entries do not.
Already listed as a Copilot surface by _TOKENSAVE_AGENT_PATHS['copilot'] in src/helpers/mcp.py, alongside the VS Code user file.

surfaces.name: Claude Code project binding
notes: The correct, already-managed shape. Command is a bare name and the path arg is a template, never an interpolated machine path - see _canonical_project_entry in src/helpers/mcp.py.

adapter_implications: Two of three surfaces already use 'mcpServers'; only the VS Code user/workspace file uses 'servers' + 'inputs'.
A 'type' field appears in the two agent surfaces but not in .mcp.json - write_servers must preserve it rather than normalising it away.
'inputs' is a sibling of 'servers' and must survive a read/write round-trip, along with any other unknown data field.
